mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial register of the investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: obtain an Apostille from the designated Competent Authority of the origin state (if it is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention). Consular Legalization route: if the origin state is not an Apostille party, obtain certification from the Korean Embassy/Consulate in that jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never perform them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry authority or competent tax office in the investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: Apostille issued by the origin state's Competent Authority. Consular Legalization route: legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission in the origin state for non-Hague parties. Mutually exclusive alternatives; no sequential combination.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the local Korean incorporator or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investing entity, notarized by a public notary in the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: Apostille from the origin state's Competent Authority. Consular Legalization route: Korean consular legalization in the origin state for non-Apostille countries. Parallel and exclusive; never used together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutive document) of the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: Apostille from the origin state's Competent Authority. Consular Legalization route: Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization for non-Hague states. Mutually exclusive; do not chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investing entity issued by a financial institution recognized under AML/CFT standards
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The investor's relationship bank, branch under the Financial Supervisory Service or equivalent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: apostillization by the origin state Competent Authority. Consular Legalization route: legalization via the Korean mission in the origin state for non-Apostille jurisdictions. Two parallel, mutually exclusive authentication paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any incorporation step, all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and shareholders must be screened against the consolidated list maintained by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, the OFAC SDN list, the EU consolidated list, and the FATF watch lists (including high-risk jurisdictions). Because the target business involves digital game publishing and payout from Steam and PlayStation, enhanced due diligence must verify the source of funds and the payment flow to ensure no connection to sanctioned regimes, designated terrorist organizations, or politically exposed persons (PEPs). For any PEP, senior-level approval, enhanced monitoring, and source-of-wealth verification are mandatory. The screening must be repeated at every change of shareholders and before entering payout contracts.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry Office (I-RO) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea at https://www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be expressed in the Korean script (Hangul). A foreign-language name may be used in trade and for the English alias, but it must be transliterated into Hangul for registration and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered trade name. The four-tier composition is: (1) optional business descriptor, (2) core trade name, (3) the corporate type suffix 'Chusik Hoesa', and (4) any required industry or license wording; the suffix must be included in Hangul. The registry compares names using Hangul text; romanized variations are not compared separately.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed company name, the applicant may, within 14 days from the notice of rejection, submit a written reconsideration request to the competent district court registry together with an explanation and any supporting trademark or prior-use evidence. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may apply for a court adjudication under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act; alternatively, the applicant may amend the name and submit a new registration application. An applicant who fails to respond within the 14-day window must re-file the name application and is not entitled to a priority date. Legal counsel should be engaged to prepare the appeal, verify conflict with similar prior names, and possibly negotiate a coexistence consent with the prior owner.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Korean Commercial Act, every stock corporation must have a principal office within the Republic of Korea and register that address with the competent district court registry. A virtual office or commercial mailbox may technically satisfy registration if a valid lease agreement and the right to use the address are documented, and some registered-agent services offer such addresses. However, the National Tax Service (NTS) and most Korean banks reject virtual offices for a profitable digital-publishing company; banks require an in-person visit, a physical signboard, and documentary proof of substantive management. The Korean tax authorities frequently cross-check the registered office address with business activity, lease contracts, and utility bills; a virtual-office address substantially increases the risk of open-ended tax investigations and the denial of corporate bank accounts. Therefore, virtual offices are permissible only as a temporary measure pending physical premises; for the planned Steam and PlayStation publishing activity, a physical office with at least one executive present is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office sign and corporate seal; (2) original lease contract and receipts; (3) payroll and social insurance records for employees; (4) accounting software and financial statements; (5) business licenses (business registration certificate, website business statement), and (6) payout contracts with Steam and PlayStation. Quantified risk: high (75%) for a newly incorporated company in the digital-content sector during the first 12 months; municipal registry inspections occur only upon complaints or anomalies, while the NTS conducts field inspections in roughly 1 in 3 new companies with low reported revenue but high bank turnover.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory rate of 0.4% of paid-in capital plus 20% education tax; estimated for nominal capital of KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal service fee for drafting incorporation documents and UBO/AML compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for private Korean stock corporation formation with foreign shareholders, including CDD and PEP screening.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization fees for foreign investor documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee schedule of the relevant origin state and Korean consular tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign company documents into Korean
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of approximately USD 50-80 per page for notarized translation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account setup and KYC compliance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 17862, as amended), Articles 288, 291, 292, 295, 297, 300, 312, 314, 317, 318, 329, 330, 331, 332, 347, and 389, together with the Regulation on Commercial Registration, the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office of the Chusik Hoesa, operated through the National Court Administration electronic registration portal of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, incorporation meeting minutes, first board meeting minutes, capital contribution deposit certificate, appointments and consents, and registered office proof, filed with the competent district court registration office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Commercial Act imposes no fixed statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa; the promoters may choose any positive aggregate subscription amount, subject to each par-value share being at least KRW 100. The full issue price of every subscribed share must be paid in cash into a bank contribution deposit account opened in the name of the company being formed before the incorporation registration is filed. The bank must issue a certificate of contribution deposit for presentation to the registration court. The deposit is not a government escrow; after registration, the funds become the company's corporate capital and are released to the operating bank account. Foreign investors who subscribe are subject to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and must file a foreign investment report where the investment reaches KRW 100 million or more, with the report obtainable through the receiving bank or KOTRA's Invest Korea one-stop service. No share withdrawal or operating payment may be made from the contribution account before registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first meeting of the board of directors of [Company] Chusik Hoesa (the Company), held on [Date] at the registered office of the Company, with all duly elected directors present in person or by electronic conference in a manner permitted by the Company's Articles of Incorporation, and with a legal quorum throughout: WHEREAS the incorporation registration of the Company has been completed and the Company has legal existence as a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS the board is authorized under Article 393 of the Commercial Act and the Company's Articles of Incorporation to resolve all matters of corporate management, capital, banking, treasury, and officer election; WHEREAS the Company's business includes the publication and distribution of PC and console video games through digital stores such as Steam and PlayStation Store, and requires multi-currency corporate bank accounts in Korea as well as designated foreign-currency settlement accounts; WHEREAS the founders have paid the full subscribed share capital into the corporate contribution deposit account and have furnished the bank's certificate of contribution deposit; and WHEREAS all directors have received a complete copy of the subscribers' register and the incorporation accounts. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The board ratifies the subscriptions and allotments set out in the subscribers' register, consisting of [Number of Shares] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW 100 each, subscribed and fully paid in cash at the aggregate price of KRW [Amount], and directs the issuance of share certificates to the subscribers and the entry of their names in the shareholders' register. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The board approves the opening of a corporate operating account and any related foreign-currency accounts with [Bank], including USD-denominated settlement accounts intended to receive Steam Valve payouts and PlayStation Store payouts. The representative director and one other director or chief financial officer designated by the representative director shall be joint signatories for payments and wire transfers, except that any single transaction exceeding US$50,000 shall require the signature of two authorized signatories. The board authorizes the execution of banking agreements, electronic banking terms, treasury mandates, and payment clearing instructions. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The board adopts the registered office located at [Address], Republic of Korea, as the sole legal seat and administrative address of the Company, and authorizes the representative director to execute and maintain the lease, the official company seal, and the corporate statutory records at that address. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The board appoints [Name] as Representative Director, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Secretary to the Board, and confirms that each appointee accepts office and is not disqualified under the Commercial Act or the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. The board further resolves to maintain a statutory auditor or an audit committee if the Company's paid-in capital or scale exceeds the statutory threshold requiring external audit. 5. DELEGATION AND EXECUTION: The board authorizes each officer to execute all applications, foreign exchange reports, contracts, and corporate filings necessary to effect these resolutions, and directs that this board resolution be entered in the corporate minute book, be certified by the Secretary, and be made available to the Company's bankers, notaries, and the competent registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters in consultation with a licensed Korean attorney, with notarization by a Korean notary public under the Notaries Public Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the promoters and resolve by unanimous consent on the exact corporate name, registered office address, business purpose, authorized share capital, par value per share, share classes, method of public notification, fiscal year, and board composition. The business purpose must expressly cover the publication and distribution of PC and console video games through online digital stores, including Steam and PlayStation Store, as well as software development, game content production, and technology ancillary services. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean and submit them to a notary public for certification after each promoter has reviewed the final text. If a legal agent or attorney-in-fact files the documents on behalf of non-resident promoters, the power of attorney must be notarized and apostilled. The certified Articles become the foundational instrument for the subsequent bank deposit and court registration steps.
required_dossiers: Promoter passports or government-issued identification
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Notarized power of attorney if filing through an agent
Promoter identity cards or corporate registration certificates for non-resident investors
Written consents of proposed directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing counsel objects to a provision, amend the relevant clause by unanimous promoters' resolution and re-notarize the corrected Articles. If a business object is considered too narrow or potentially ultra vires, broaden the object clause to cover digital content publishing, game development, electronic commerce, and licensing, then obtain a fresh notarial certification before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of paid-in capital and issuance of contribution deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea, with KOTRA Invest Korea and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy only if a foreign investment report is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate contribution deposit account in the name of the company being formed, deposit the full issue price of each subscribed share from every promoter or subscriber, and obtain the bank's certificate of contribution deposit. The certificate must be addressed to the company and must confirm the account name, the amount deposited, the date of deposit, and the bank's undertaking not to return the contribution funds before the completion of incorporation registration. If any subscriber is a non-resident investor, the bank branch will process the foreign exchange receipt and, if the investment threshold is met, file the foreign investment report with KOTRA through the one-stop service. No part of the deposited capital may be disbursed before registration. The certificate must be retained and submitted with the registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscribed shares schedule with exact amounts
Source-of-funds evidence and AML/KYC forms
Passports or corporate IDs of all paying subscribers
Bank account application for the company under formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the source of funds, provide supplemental bank statements, tax returns, sale documents, or audited financial evidence as requested by the bank's compliance division. If the bank declines to issue the certificate, close the temporary account and open a new contribution account with another authorized foreign exchange bank, then obtain the required certificate before the registration window expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Holding of incorporation general meeting and appointment of directors, representative director, and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters and subscribers at the incorporation general meeting, followed by the first meeting of the board of directors, governed by Commercial Act Articles 312 through 316, 318, and 389
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After all shares have been fully paid, convene the incorporation general meeting at which the promoters report the subscribed capital, present the bank's certificate of contribution deposit, and confirm the paid-in amount. The subscribers then elect the first directors and, where required by the Company's scale, a statutory auditor. Immediately following the incorporators' meeting, the newly elected directors hold the first board meeting to appoint the representative director, the chief financial officer, and the secretary to the board, and to approve the board resolutions on share allotment, banking, registered office adoption, and signing authorities. Complete minutes must be prepared in Korean, signed by the chairperson and attending directors or shareholders, and dated. The minutes become part of the registration dossier and must reflect the exact names and identity documents of all appointed officers.
required_dossiers: Notice of incorporation general meeting or signed waiver of notice
Bank certificate of contribution deposit
Subscriber register and payment confirmations
Minutes of the incorporation general meeting
Minutes of the first board meeting
Written acceptances of office signed by directors, auditor, and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is challenged for lack of quorum or notice, reconvene the meeting with all subscribers or obtain a unanimous written resolution curing the defect. If the minutes contain an error in the officer names or in the signing authority, adopt a confirmatory board resolution and attach it to the corrected minutes before the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the competent district court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court of the Company's registered office, with electronic filing through the National Court Administration registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after the incorporation procedure is completed, submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company to the competent district court registry. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, incorporation general meeting minutes, first board meeting minutes, bank contribution certificate, subscription schedule, lease proof for the registered office, and appointment consents. The registry will assess the registration tax and court fee, review the filed dossiers, and issue the corporation registration number and the certified registration record. Electronic filing requires the applicant or a registered legal representative to log in to the National Court Administration portal, upload the documents, and pay the prescribed fees. After approval, obtain a certified copy of the corporate register and the certificate of registration details. These documents constitute the Company's legal confirmation of existence and are needed for business registration, banking, and store agreements.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of incorporation general meeting and first board meeting
Certificate of contribution deposit
Subscriptions list and payment confirmations
Certificate or contract proving the registered office address
Written consents and identity documents of directors, auditor, and representative director
Power of attorney if filing through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary order, produce the requested document, such as a missing lease certificate or certified copy of the notarial deed, within the prescribed time under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. If the registration application is rejected, cure the stated defect and refile promptly; if the rejection is legally incorrect, an immediate appeal may be filed with the higher registration court.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea; electronic compliance portal: HomeTax Integrated Tax Portal at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing or owning a Korean Chusik Hoesa must obtain a Business Registration Certificate from the local district tax office of the corporation's place of business through the HomeTax electronic filing system. The procedure comprises: (1) incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act and issue of the corporate registration certificate; (2) submission of the business registration application to the National Tax Service within 20 days of business commencement through HomeTax or directly at the competent tax office; (3) attendance of the articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, proof of business establishment, and identification of the statutory representative; (4) issuance by the NTS of a 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves simultaneously as the Tax Identification Number, Corporate Tax number, withholding account number, and Value-Added Tax identification number; and (5) for a foreign-owned Korean entity, appointment of a domestic tax representative if required under the Framework Act on National Taxes for service of process and tax correspondence. For a non-resident foreign corporation without a domestic establishment but supplying electronic services in Korea, the NTS applies the separate non-resident business registration function on HomeTax, assigning a VAT identification number and requiring a domestic tax representative where called for by the Value-Added Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korean tax law does not provide check-the-box or elective pass-through classification for a Chusik Hoesa. The entity is mandatorily taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, and Korea applies anti-hybrid rules through the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, but no elective classification mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All businesses supplying taxable goods or services in Korea are obliged to register for VAT; there is no general exemption threshold for registered corporations, but simplified taxpayer treatment may apply where annual taxable turnover does not exceed KRW 80,000,000. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services, including digital game publishing and platform-based sales, are required to register for VAT through HomeTax regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean VAT law mandates the issuance of an Electronic Tax Invoice for every business-to-business tax invoice transaction. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax e-invoice system by the end of the day following issuance, which operates as a near-real-time fiscal clearance and cross-matching requirement. Taxpayers may transmit via HomeTax directly or through NTS-approved EDI/API interfaces. Korea does not use a cryptographic anti-fraud tax stamp; instead, the NTS enforces the mandate through e-invoice matching, mandatory cash receipt issuance for final consumers, and periodic VAT return verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating under the Value-Added Tax Act applies to supplies of exported goods, to services supplied to non-resident foreign recipients for use outside Korea, and to qualifying electronic services supplied to non-resident consumers, including downloadable PC/console game content sold through platforms such as Steam and PlayStation Store. To substantiate the zero rate, the Korean vendor must prove that the customer is a foreign resident, the service is treated as consumed abroad, and the export sales proceeds are actually collected in foreign currency and legally repatriated to Korea. The statutory evidence required includes customs export declarations for physical goods and, for digital publishing, platform payout statements and foreign exchange settlement records showing repatriation of the remittances from Valve, Sony Interactive Entertainment, or similar platform operators.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Export Declaration Certificate issued through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physically exported goods
Commercial Invoice and Packing List in international sales format
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation / Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency
Steam or PlayStation Store sales reconciliation and settlement reports showing transactions by country, transaction identifiers, net amounts, and payer details
Electronic evidence of the foreign customer's residence, including billing address, payment instrument country, and digital delivery records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service audits zero-rated export claims by cross-referencing customs export records, foreign exchange settlement data, and digital platform payout records. Where documentary substantiation is missing or inadequate, the NTS assesses VAT at the statutory 10% rate with default additional tax and interest from the original filing period. Fraudulent or misleading claims trigger penalty taxes up to 40% of the avoided VAT, voiding of refund positions, extension of the clawback statute of limitations to 10 years, and potential criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), the principal foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but strictly reporting-based foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, supervised by the Bank of Korea. The Korean won is freely convertible for bona fide current account transactions, including royalties from Steam and PlayStation Store sales, commission payments, and dividend remittances, provided the remitting bank receives an underlying contract and a valid foreign exchange purpose code. Capital account transactions are not freely convertible: any non-resident equity injection, shareholder loan, or acquisition of local securities must be reported through a domestic dealing bank to the Bank of Korea, and transactions above the statutory threshold require prior approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The Bank of Korea does not impose mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds; however, all foreign currency receipts must be collected into a Korean foreign exchange bank account within the statutory collection period. Profit repatriation from a Chusik Hoesa is permitted after corporate income tax has been paid, evidenced by a tax clearance certificate and a board resolution declaring the dividend, but the remitting bank must verify the original foreign investment report, the withholding tax payment, and the equivalent capital account reporting before releasing the proceeds to the overseas shareholder.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received into a Korean foreign exchange bank account within six months from the export date for goods, or within six months from the completion of services for digital publishing. The statutory mandatory conversion ratio to KRW is 0%, meaning the exporter may hold the foreign currency without any requirement to surrender it to the Bank of Korea or any state-designated bank. The collecting bank must verify the export customs declaration, the platform settlement statement, the SWIFT credit advice, and the commercial invoice. If the six-month window cannot be met, an extension must be requested from the head of the dealing bank, and any extension exceeding the approval authority must be submitted to the Bank of Korea.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for paid-in capital and foreign direct investment reporting
Foreign Currency Settlement Account for platform royalties

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs without a Bank of Korea foreign exchange banking license are legally barred from serving as the primary treasury institution for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. A Korean entity's inbound SWIFT payments and outbound trade remittances must clear through a resident dealing bank, and the foreign exchange reporting obligations of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act cannot be fulfilled by a non-bank EMI. Such providers may be considered only as ancillary collection tools, but the full account infrastructure, capital escrow, and FX hedging must remain with domestically licensed tier-1 commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and the UBO must physically appear at a Korean commercial bank branch to execute corporate onboarding for a new Chusik Hoesa. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted. In exceptional cases where all directors are non-resident, an apostilled power of attorney and a signed board resolution can authorize a local representative to conduct the KYC interview, but at least one director must complete a video call with the bank's compliance officer and the original corporate documents must be delivered in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected third-party royalty routing: all Steam and PlayStation revenues arrive via foreign payment processors rather than direct contractual counterparty remittances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original distribution agreements with Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment, official platform payout statements, a letter from the payment processor identifying the ultimate source of funds, and a signed treasury undertaking listing the contractual counterparties, transaction purpose, and expected inbound amount band.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by a chain of non-resident nominee shareholders or a family trust structure unusual for a digital game publisher
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate organigram, notarized ownership chart, identity documents and passport copies for every natural person holding more than 10%, board resolution authorizing the account opening, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent, and the Korean tax registration certificate confirming actual business operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared ISIC code 5820 publishing scope and continuous large outbound payments for outsourced code development, marketing, or platform commissions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed software development contracts, per-project cost schedules, VAT invoices, transfer pricing documentation in line with Korean TP rules, and a profit attribution policy explaining why a portion of gross revenue is paid to international developers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX purpose-code ambiguity: inbound capital contributions and outbound royalty payments contain inconsistent SWIFT purpose descriptions, triggering Bank of Korea reporting and anti-money laundering concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-prescribed foreign exchange report forms for each transaction class, a reconciliation ledger matching every SWIFT MT103 with the corresponding commercial invoice or shareholder loan agreement, and written confirmation from the licensed dealing bank that all reports have been transmitted to the Bank of Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity capital for the Chusik Hoesa must be received only through a domestic dealing bank and reported to the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act as a direct investment. The SWIFT wire must include the proper purpose code, for example Investment - Equity Capital, together with the entity's corporate registration number. After the funds are credited to the capital escrow account, the bank issues a foreign direct investment report certificate and the company files the paid-in capital registration with the Korean court. All inbound wires should avoid personal accounts and intermediary banks that cannot support purpose-code transparency, and the bank-issued inward remittance certificate is the primary capital verification document.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the game publishing business should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for platform royalties, marketing, and licensing fees, because these transactions are intangible and invoice-driven. For high-value software development or advisory contracts where goods and services are bundled, a documentary collection or a commercial letter of credit may be used to give the counterparty a bank-backed payment undertaking. All MT103 messages must be transmitted through the Korean head-office SWIFT network with the relevant revenue type code and a copy of the underlying agreement retained in the treasury file for Bank of Korea audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with domestic Korean banks for underlying USD/KRW exposure arising from committed revenue streams, capped at 100% of the anticipated invoice amount

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) participation only through onshore dealing banks where the entity has a documented real underlying exposure; offshore NDFs are not permitted for a Korean resident Chusik Hoesa

Cross-currency swaps for long-term foreign direct investment liabilities or shareholder subordinated loans, subject to Bank of Korea restrictions on speculative derivative transactions by small corporations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate record maintained at the registered head office; no government filing required unless followed by court registration of officer changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the regular general meeting without just cause are subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act; no automatic strike-off, but persistent failure can trigger court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor appointment resolution for companies meeting the statutory audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Recorded in shareholders' meeting minutes; appointment notified through the Financial Supervisory Service external audit system by the appointed auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor exposes the company to Financial Supervisory Service administrative orders and penalty fines; an invalid audit appointment may nullify the statutory audit report.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audit report and audited annual financial statements submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the External Audit Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the ordinary general meeting approving the financial statements; for a June 30 general meeting, by July 14
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty surcharges apply for failure to submit the audit report; persistent violations may result in FSS sanctions, public disclosure of the violation, and restrictions on corporate filing capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and local income tax surcharge return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and the competent local government through the integrated tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following a December 31 fiscal year-end; a one-month extension may apply when taxable income is computed by a licensed tax preparer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported tax is penalized at 20 percent, or 40 percent for fraudulent non-reporting; under-reported tax is penalized at 10 percent; late payment interest accrues at 0.022 percent per day; continued delinquency can lead to National Tax Service business registration cancellation and judicial strike-off or dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration of re-elected directors and statutory officers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent district court registry through the Supreme Court Electronic Registration System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the general meeting or board resolution approving the officer change; for a June 30 general meeting, by July 14
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered changes are not opposable to bona fide third parties; late registration may attract a fine of up to KRW 5 million under commercial registration rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report for share transfers involving foreign beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through Invest KOREA or a designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the share transfer or any change in the foreign ownership ratio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violations of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may carry administrative fines of up to KRW 5 million; failure to report may restrict the foreign investor's access to foreign investment protection and incentives.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions include the special tax credits for research and development expenditure under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, the tax credit for increasing new investment in productivity facilities, and the SME (Small and Medium Enterprise) tax deduction of 5% to 30% from corporate income tax for qualifying small and medium corporations under Article 7 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act. Additionally, the tax credit for job creation and the foreign-invested enterprise tax holiday under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1120-1 (Beobinsaebeopsehwagwan) for the Korean corporate income tax return, filed through the National Tax Service's HomeTax electronic filing system (hometax.go.kr), or the established electronic filing service of the National Tax Information System.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The statutory deadline is three months after the end of the fiscal year for the annual corporate income tax return. If the fiscal year ends on December 31, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. For a non-resident corporation with no domestic business place, the return is due within two months after the end of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification particulars: registered trade name, corporate registration number, business registration number, fiscal year-end date, and resident representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation must enter its Korean business place registration number or its OID (on-line integrated registration) number, the foreign corporate name, and the resident agent's details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue or sales amount from the relevant business year, including license fees, royalties, and digital store publishing revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident digital game publisher must report all Korean-source income from Steam and PlayStation Store sales, including user-payment-derived royalties and distribution proceeds attributable to the Korean market.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses and cost of goods sold, including development costs, platform commissions, payment processing fees, marketing expenses, and royalties paid to third-party licensors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation must substantiate expenses with Korean tax invoices or equivalent foreign documentation; expense deductions are restricted to items directly connected to domestic-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculation after application of non-deductible expenses and tax-exempt income adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a branch, compute taxable income under Article 95 of the Corporate Income Tax Act using the deemed calculation or actual account settlement election; consider the deemed income rate for a foreign corporation without a domestic place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base after deducting loss carryforwards and special tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation may apply only domestic-source loss carryforwards within the five-year limit and treaty non-discrimination provisions if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax amount calculated on the income base: 10% from KRW 0 to KRW 200 million, 20% on the portion exceeding KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, and 22% for the portion exceeding KRW 20 billion plus the local income tax surtax of 10% of the corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident branch must also pay the local income tax surtax and file the corresponding local tax return with the competent local government or the National Tax Service designated platform.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits claimed, including the research and development credit, foreign tax credit, and exemption/reduction credits under tax treaty provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation must attach the treaty relief application and the foreign tax credit calculation table, along with the Certificate of Tax Residence (COR) issued by the home country tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a corporate income tax return by the statutory deadline triggers a non-filing penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid tax amount, or 0.5% per day of the unpaid tax amount after the overdue period, subject to a minimum of KRW 100,000. Additionally, a negligence penalty of 10% of the underreported tax and a 0.03% monthly surcharge for late payment, aggregating to 3.3% per annum, may apply. For failure to submit the local income tax surtax return, an additional penalty equivalent to 10% of the unpaid local income tax is imposed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident recipient must submit the Application for Exemption from or Reduction of Withholding Tax Under Tax Treaties (Form 34-24) to the Korean withholding agent before the payment date, together with a Certificate of Tax Residence (COR) issued by the tax authority of the jurisdiction of residence, endorsed by the competent authority, and attested by apostille if required. The withholding agent shall then apply the reduced treaty rate. Alternatively, a refund application may be filed with the competent district tax office within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the tax arose, and the National Tax Service shall process the refund after review. For a payment between a Korean corporation and its parent, the Korea Morphology test may be applied to confirm the beneficial owner and business substance of the recipient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For royalties for the use of intellectual property, the statutory withholding tax rate is 22% (20% corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax). Under the OECD-based Korea tax treaties, the royalty withholding rate is generally reduced to 10-15%; for example, the Korea-Japan treaty allows 10%, Korea-US treaty allows 10% for royalties, and Korea-China treaty allows 10% for royalties. For interest income, the statutory withholding tax rate is 22%, treaty reduced rates commonly range from 5% to 15%, and Korea's treaties with major trading partners typically reduce the interest rate to 10% or 5% for financial institutions and specific government instruments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) or more in total gross revenue; however, a mandatory Local File must be prepared if the corporation's related party cross-border transactions exceed or are expected to exceed KRW 10 billion in aggregate, and Master File preparation is mandatory when the revenue is KRW 100 billion or more and the intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 10 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the economic substance doctrine through Article 15 of the Framework Act on Local Taxation and the corporate income tax anti-avoidance rules in the Corporate Income Tax Act, including the substance-over-form principle. For international tax matters, the OECD BEPS actions and a general anti-abuse rule deny treaty benefits to structures lacking business purpose and economic substance. Additionally, a Korean resident or domestic corporation must report to the Ministry of Economy and Finance any foreign financial account with a balance of KRW 500 million or more, and a shell company or conduit entity without substantial economic activities may be disregarded for treaty relief under the Limitation on Benefits clause or the principal purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Korean-source digital store revenue from the corporate income tax return, underreporting Steam or PlayStation sales allocated to Korean users, fabricating deductions, or manipulating the accounting books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of imprisonment up to 10 years, or a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax amount (Optionally up to 50 times the annual tax amount), plus underreporting penalties of 10% to 40% of the unreported tax and a 3.3% annual surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally or negligently participated may be personally jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the National Tax Collection Act; the court may impose criminal imprisonment; travel bans may be issued by the Commissioner of the National Tax Service; and the director's personal assets may be subject to collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or operating a Korean Chusik Hoesa with no substantive game publishing business, no local office, no employees, and no economic substance solely to route royalties or dividends to a low-tax jurisdiction or to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty withholding tax relief, recharacterization of the transaction, 40% penalty on the understated tax amount, and cancellation of the corporate registration. Under the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination, the National Tax Service may impose a 30% penalty on the amount of tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for the reconstruction of income and the payment of aggregate penalties; if the shell company is used to launder funds, anti-money laundering sanctions apply with imprisonment up to 5 years for the responsible officers; courts may issue asset freezes against the directors and order the disclosure and confiscation of hidden proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to declare a foreign financial account (including a Steam or PlayStation payment account balance) held by the Korean corporation or its director or beneficial owner when the aggregate balance exceeds KRW 500 million, or using undisclosed offshore accounts to receive digital store payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to KRW 200 million for foreign account reporting violations; under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, the violation attracts additional sanctions and the proceeds of the crime may be confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director is subject to the criminal fines or imprisonment; the National Tax Service may impose a personal entity tax liability for assets owned by the director if corporate assets are diverted; a travel ban and departure prohibition under the Immigration Act will apply during tax and criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a false corporate income tax return with forged foreign tax credit certificates, fabricated VAT invoices, or falsely claiming treaty exemption for royalties paid to a related resident partner of a treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to KRW 100 million; the false declaration triggers a 40% penalty on the underreported tax, plus 10% of the falsely claimed tax credits; and revocation of beneficial tax treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false filing may be personally liable for the penalty and the additional corporate tax; criminal conviction may bar the director from serving as a registered officer of any company for up to 5 years; civil recovery of the government damages may be pursued in addition to the criminal fines.
